problem.summary: 现有视觉识别框架（如ResNet、VGGNet）采用串联的高到低分辨率卷积来编码低分辨率表示，然后从低分辨率表示中恢复高分辨率表示。这种方法在位置敏感的视觉任务（如人体姿态估计、语义分割、目标检测）中存在局限性，因为恢复的高分辨率表示在语义丰富性和空间精确性上不足。

motivation.summary: 高分辨率表示对于位置敏感的视觉问题至关重要。现有方法通过串联卷积降低分辨率再恢复，导致信息损失和空间细节丢失。需要一种能全程保持高分辨率表示的网络架构，以同时获得语义丰富性和空间精确性。

core_idea.summary: 提出高分辨率网络（HRNet），其核心思想是：（1）将高到低分辨率的卷积流并行连接，而非串联；（2）在整个网络过程中维持高分辨率表示；（3）通过重复的多分辨率融合模块交换跨分辨率信息，从而生成语义更丰富、空间更精确的表示。

method.summary: HRNet由四个阶段组成。第一阶段包含高分辨率卷积。后续阶段逐步添加高到低分辨率的并行流，并通过多分辨率融合模块重复交换信息。网络主干包括并行多分辨率卷积、重复的多分辨率融合和表示头。具体架构细节见附录A的表14。

experiments.summary: 在多个视觉任务上进行了广泛实验：人体姿态估计（COCO数据集）、语义分割（Cityscapes、PASCAL-Context、LIP数据集）、目标检测（COCO数据集）以及面部关键点检测（WFLW、AFLW、COFW、300W数据集）。实验结果表明HRNet在各项任务上均优于现有方法。

claims.claim: HRNet通过并行连接高到低分辨率卷积流并重复融合信息，能全程保持高分辨率表示。
HRNet生成的表示语义更丰富、空间更精确，适用于位置敏感的视觉任务。
HRNet在人体姿态估计、语义分割、目标检测等多个任务上达到或超越了现有最佳方法。

limitations.limitation: 论文未明确讨论HRNet的局限性。潜在的局限性可能包括：并行多分辨率流增加了模型复杂性和计算开销；对于某些简单任务，HRNet可能过于复杂；论文主要关注视觉识别任务，未探索其他领域（如自然语言处理）的应用。

nodes.title: 输入图像与主干
nodes.label: 输入处理
nodes.summary: 输入图像经过主干网络（stem），该主干由两个步长为2的3×3卷积组成，将分辨率降低到1/4。
nodes.description: 主干网络（stem）负责初步特征提取和分辨率降低。它由两个步长为2的3×3卷积层组成，将输入图像的空间分辨率降低到原始尺寸的1/4。

nodes.title: 并行多分辨率卷积流
nodes.label: 并行卷积
nodes.summary: 网络主体包含多个并行的卷积流，每个流处理不同分辨率的特征图。从高分辨率流开始，逐步添加高到低分辨率的流。
nodes.description: HRNet的核心结构是并行连接的多分辨率卷积流。第一阶段仅包含高分辨率卷积流。在后续阶段，逐步添加新的、分辨率更低的卷积流，所有流并行处理。每个流由多个残差单元组成。

nodes.title: 多分辨率融合模块
nodes.label: 信息融合
nodes.summary: 在每个阶段内和阶段之间，通过多分辨率融合模块重复交换不同分辨率流之间的信息。
nodes.description: 多分辨率融合模块负责在不同分辨率的特征图之间交换信息。它通过下采样（步长卷积）和上采样（双线性插值或1×1卷积）操作，将信息从一个分辨率流聚合到其他分辨率流。这种融合在每个模块化块内重复进行。

nodes.title: 表示头
nodes.label: 输出表示
nodes.summary: 网络的输出表示头根据具体任务（如姿态估计、分割）生成最终预测。对于不同任务，表示头的设计不同。
nodes.description: 表示头是网络的最后部分，负责将多分辨率特征图转换为特定任务的输出。例如，对于人体姿态估计，它生成热图；对于语义分割，它生成分割图。论文中提到了HRNetV1、HRNetV2和HRNetV2p等变体，对应不同的表示头设计。

nodes.title: 网络阶段与模块化块
nodes.label: 网络架构
nodes.summary: HRNet由四个阶段组成，每个阶段包含重复的模块化块。每个模块化块由多个分支（对应不同分辨率）和融合单元构成。
nodes.description: 网络主体分为四个阶段。第一阶段只有高分辨率分支。第二、三、四阶段分别包含二、三、四个分辨率分支。每个阶段由重复的模块化块组成（第一、二阶段重复1次，第三阶段重复4次，第四阶段重复3次）。每个模块化块包含多个残差单元和一个融合单元。

edges.label: 特征输入
edges.description: 主干网络输出的1/4分辨率特征图作为并行多分辨率卷积流的输入。

edges.label: 特征提供
edges.description: 并行卷积流生成的多分辨率特征图被送入多分辨率融合模块进行信息交换。

edges.label: 信息反馈
edges.description: 融合后的特征图被反馈回对应的并行卷积流，用于后续的特征提取。

edges.label: 特征输出
edges.description: 最终阶段的并行卷积流输出的多分辨率特征图被送入表示头生成任务特定的预测。

edges.label: 结构定义
edges.description: 网络阶段与模块化块的结构定义了并行卷积流的组织方式和重复模式。

edges.label: 融合安排
edges.description: 网络阶段与模块化块的结构决定了多分辨率融合模块的插入位置和频率。

deltas.before: 串联的高到低分辨率卷积流，先降低分辨率再恢复。
deltas.after: 并行的高到低分辨率卷积流，全程保持高分辨率。
deltas.why_it_matters: 避免了分辨率降低和恢复过程中的信息损失，能够同时保持高空间分辨率和丰富的语义信息，这对于位置敏感的任务（如姿态估计、分割）至关重要。

deltas.before: 高分辨率表示通过解码器从低分辨率表示中恢复。
deltas.after: 高分辨率表示在网络前向传播过程中始终存在并被逐步增强。
deltas.why_it_matters: 生成的表示在空间上更精确，因为高分辨率特征从未丢失，减少了上采样带来的模糊和误差。

deltas.before: 多尺度特征融合通常在网络末端或特定模块中进行一次。
deltas.after: 多分辨率融合模块在每个阶段内和阶段之间重复多次进行。
deltas.why_it_matters: 重复的融合使得不同分辨率的特征能够充分交互，增强了表示的语义丰富性和上下文感知能力。

glossary.表示头: 网络末端的模块，将多分辨率特征图转换为特定任务的输出，如热图（姿态估计）或分割图（语义分割）。
glossary.HRNetV1: HRNet的一个变体，其表示头仅使用最高分辨率的特征图进行预测。
glossary.HRNetV2: HRNet的一个变体，其表示头将所有分辨率的特征图拼接后进行预测。
glossary.HRNetV2p: HRNet的一个变体，用于目标检测，其表示头生成多尺度特征金字塔。
glossary.模块化块: HRNet每个阶段的基本构建单元，包含多个残差单元和一个融合单元。
glossary.残差单元: 卷积块，通常包含两个3×3卷积层和一个跳跃连接，用于特征提取。
glossary.步长卷积: 步长为2的卷积操作，用于降低特征图的空间分辨率。
glossary.上采样: 增加特征图空间分辨率的操作，本文中主要使用双线性插值或1×1卷积。

metadata.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

metadata.abstract: High-resolution representations are essential for position-sensitive vision problems, such as human pose estimation, semantic segmentation, and object detection. Existing state-of-the-art frameworks first encode the input image as a low-resolution representation through a subnetwork that is formed by connecting high-to-low resolution convolutions in series (e.g., ResNet, VGGNet), and then recover the high-resolution representation from the encoded low-resolution representation. Instead, our proposed network, named as High-Resolution Network (HRNet), maintains high-resolution representations through the whole process. There are two key characteristics: (i) Connect the high-to-low resolution convolution streams in parallel and (ii) repeatedly exchange the information across resolutions. The benefit is that the resulting representation is semantically richer and spatially more precise. We show the superiority of the proposed HRNet in a wide range of applications, including human pose estimation, semantic segmentation, and object detection, suggesting that the HRNet is a stronger backbone for computer vision problems. All the codes are available at https://github.com/HRNet.

3.3 Representation Head

We have three kinds of representation heads that are illus- trated in Figure 4, and call them as HRNetV 1, HRNetV 2, and HRNetV1p, respectively. HRNetV1. The output is the representation only from the high-resolution stream. Other three representations are ig- nored. This is illustrated in Figure 4 (a). HRNetV2. We rescale the low-resolution representations through bilinear upsampling without changing the number of channels to the high resolution, and concatenate the four representations, followed by a 1× 1 convolution to mix the four representations. This is illustrated in Figure 4 (b). HRNetV2p. We construct multi-level representations by downsampling the high-resolution representation output from HRNetV 2 to multiple levels. This is depicted in Fig- ure 4 (c). In this paper, we will show the results of applying HRNetV1 to human pose estimation, HRNetV 2 to semantic segmentation, and HRNetV2p to object detection.
3.4 Instantiation

The main body contains four stages with four parallel con- volution streams. The resolutions are 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, and 1/32. The ﬁrst stage contains 4 residual units where each unit is formed by a bottleneck with the width 64, and is followed by one 3× 3 convolution changing the width of feature maps to C. The 2nd, 3rd, 4th stages contain 1, 4, 3 modularized blocks, respectively. Each branch in multi- resolution parallel convolution of the modularized block contains 4 residual units. Each unit contains two 3× 3 convolutions for each resolution, where each convolution is followed by batch normalization and the nonlinear ac- tivation ReLU. The widths (numbers of channels) of the convolutions of the four resolutions are C, 2C, 4C, and 8C, respectively. An example is depicted in Figure 2.

We analyze the modularized block that is divided into two components: multi-resolution parallel convolutions (Fig- ure 5 (a)), and multi-resolution fusion (Figure 5 (b)). It divides the input channels into several sub- sets of channels and performs a regular convolution over each subset over different spatial resolutions separately, while in the group convolution, the resolutions are the same. This connection implies that the multi-resolution parallel convolution enjoys some beneﬁt of the group convolution. 8 C ONCLUSIONS

In this paper, we present a high-resolution network for visual recognition problems. There are three fundamen- tal differences from existing low-resolution classiﬁcation networks and high-resolution representation learning net- works: (i) Connect high and low resolution convolutions in parallel other than in series; (ii) Maintain high resolution through the whole process instead of recovering high reso- lution from low resolution; and (iii) Fuse multi-resolution representations repeatedly, rendering rich high-resolution representations with strong position sensitivity. The superior results on a wide range of visual recog- nition problems suggest that our proposed HRNet is a stronger backbone for computer vision problems. IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON PATTERN ANAL YSIS AND MACHINE INTELLIGENCE, MARCH 2020 19 APPENDIX D FACIAL LANDMARK DETECTION Facial landmark detection a.k.a. face alignment is a problem of detecting the keypoints from a face image. We perform the evaluation over four standard datasets: WFLW [149], AFLW [75], COFW [10], and 300W [121]. We mainly use the normalized mean error (NME) for evaluation. We use the inter-ocular distance as normalization for WFLW, COFW, and 300W, and the face bounding box as normalization for AFLW. We also report area-under-the-curve scores (AUC) and failure rates. We follow the standard scheme [149] for training. All the faces are cropped by the provided boxes according to the center location and resized to 256× 256. We augment the data by±30 degrees in-plane rotation, 0.75− 1.25 scaling, and randomly ﬂipping. The base learning rate is 0.0001 and is dropped to 0.00001 and 0.000001 at the 30th and 50th epochs. At testing, each keypoint location is predicted by transforming the highest heatvalue location from 1/4 to the original

image space and adjusting it with a quarter offset in the direction from the highest response to the second highest response [23]. We adopt HRNetV2-W18 for face landmark detection whose parameter and computation cost are similar to or smaller
than models with widely-used backbones: ResNet- 50 and Hourglass [105]. HRNetV 2-W18: #parameters = 9.3M, GFLOPs
= 4 .3G; ResNet- 50: #parameters = 25 .0M, GFLOPs = 3 .8G; Hourglass: #parameters = 25 .1M, GFLOPs = 19 .1G. The

numbers are obtained on the input size 256× 256. It should be noted that the facial landmark detection methods adopting ResNet-50 and Hourglass as backbones introduce extra parameter and computation overhead. WFLW. The WFLW dataset [149] is a recently-built dataset based on the WIDER Face [164]. There are 7, 500 training and
2, 500 testing images with 98 manual annotated landmarks. We report the results on the test set and several subsets: large
pose (326 images), expression (314 images), illumination (698 images), make-up (206 images), occlusion (736 images) and
blur (773 images).
Table 20 provides the comparison of our method with state-of-the-art methods. Our approach is signiﬁcantly better

than other methods on the test set and all the subsets, including LAB that exploits extra boundary information [149] and PDB that uses stronger data augmentation [40]. AFLW. The AFLW [75] dataset is a widely used benchmark dataset, where each image has 19 facial landmarks. Following [149], [191], we train our models on 20, 000 training images, and report the results on the AFLW-Full set ( 4, 386 testing images) and the AFLW-Frontal set (1314 testing images selected from 4386 testing images).
Table 21 provides the comparison of our method with state-of-the-art methods. Our approach achieves the best

performance among methods without extra information and stronger data augmentation and even outperforms DCFE with extra 3D information. Our approach performs slightly worse than LAB that uses extra boundary information [149] and PDB [40] that uses stronger data augmentation. COFW. The COFW dataset [10] consists of 1, 345 training and 507 testing faces with occlusions, where each image has 29 facial landmarks.
Table 22 provides the comparison of our method with state-of-the-art methods. HRNetV 2 outperforms other methods
by a large margin. In particular, it achieves the better performance than LAB with extra boundary information and PDB

with stronger data augmentation. 300W. The dataset [121] is a combination of HELEN [80], LFPW [5], AFW [193], XM2VTS and IBUG datasets, where each face has 68 landmarks. Following [117], we use the 3, 148 training images, which contains the training subsets of HELEN and LFPW and the full set of AFW. We evaluate the performance using two protocols, full set and test set. The full set contains 689 images and is further divided into a common subset ( 554 images) from HELEN and LFPW, and a challenging subset (135 images) from IBUG. The ofﬁcial test set, used for competition, contains600 images (300 indoor and 300 outdoor images).
Table 23 provides the results on the full set, and its two subsets: common and challenging. Table 24 provides the results
on the test set. In comparison to Chen et al. [23] that uses Hourglass with large parameter and computation complexity

as the backbone, our scores are better except the AUC 0.08 scores. Our HRNetV2 gets the overall best performance among methods without extra information and stronger data augmentation, and is even better than LAB with extra boundary information and DCFE [141] that explores extra 3D information.
